newsitem.title: UK: Wassall shares soar on General Cable float.
newsitem.headline: Wassall shares soar on General Cable float.

text.p: Shares in diversified industrial company Wassall Plc jumped over nine percent on Monday after the company said it would float at least 70 percent of General Cable Corporation in the U.S. and return around 150 million stg to shareholders as it announced annual results.
Wassall shares were up 32 pence to 386 by 0855 GMT.
"They bought General Cable in 1994 at a valuation of $150 million and the float values it at $750 million, that's a big announcement," said one analyst.
"They can bring all that cash in and then buy something else," the analyst said.
Wassall said it planned to float the General Cable stake through an initial public offering (ipo).
Chief executive Christopher Miller said in a statement that it was "an outstanding return on our investment of only three years ago."
Final offer price and exact number of shares to be offered in General Cable will not be fixed until the end of the offer period, which is likely to be during May, the company said.
"The General Cable float was totally unexpected. I knew they would be looking to sell things off but I wasn't expecting so much so fast," the analyst said.
Wassall also said that pre-tax profits were up 27 percent in 1996 to 65.9 million stg, excluding the impact from the volatile copper price during parts of the year.
Wassall said it would pay a total dividend of 7.1 pence per share, up from 5.5 pence a year ago.
